No ratings, market quotes, presentations or call transcripts; context ratings and quotes blank
Tornado: business interruption and recoveries above inventory cost are explicitly not recognized (Q3 10-Q page:17); the net insurance outcome is open

Management claims are unverified against filings: "strongest sales growth ever" for FAM (Q3 release page:1), "record adjusted EBITDA and margins" (Q2 release page:1) and expectation that inventory losses are "fully recoverable" (Q3 release page:1) are attributed claims only

The release states debt matures "on a staggered basis through 2033" (Q3 release page:3); the Term Loan B is seven years from April 3, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:13); the maturity table prints only through 2030 and "Thereafter" (page:14)

Subsequent events after September 30, 2026 are limited to the October 23, 2026 receivables amendment, the November 4, 2026 sale of a held-for-sale North American facility, and the November 4, 2026 dividend declaration of 0.10 per share payable December 18, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:22, page:23, page:28); sale proceeds Not supplied
Image, chart and speaker-note content: none exists in the pack; not claimed

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported-basis measures built here are lower quality than management's: operating profit plus depreciation and amortization (with the 411.9 FY2025 goodwill impairment added back) gives trailing EBITDA of 210.0 at Q3 2026, so total debt to EBITDA is 4.65x and net debt to EBITDA is 4.19x, with EBITDA to cash interest of 2.62x. These are above management's 3.8x because the credit agreement and management adjusted EBITDA add back items such as stock compensation, restructuring, financing fees on the receivables program and purchase-accounting items; that definition is not supplied, so the two cannot be reconciled and neither is restated into the other. Evidence to risk to implication: a lender that sizes debt on the adjusted figure sees a levered but compliant credit; a lender that sizes it on reported earnings sees a leverage multiple that only recently dropped below five times, which makes the 2029 notes refinancing and the covenant step-downs the focus.

facts.label: Cash flow quality and earnings quality
facts.text: Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of 117.4 rose 2.9 from 114.5 (10-Q Q3 page:28), but the mix is weaker than the headline: net working capital provided 11.9 against 35.3, cash taxes were a net refund of 2.2 against 9.4 paid, and Q3 operating cash flow was 48.5 against 72.8 in the prior-year quarter (10-Q Q3 page:4, page:5, page:24). Adjusted EBITDA adds back financing fees on the Receivables Sales Agreement of 5.1 for nine months 2026 (Release Q3 page:10, page:11), stock compensation, restructuring and tornado costs, so management's measure treats the cost of selling receivables as interest. Restructuring and other impairment expense fell to 4.7 for nine months from 18.2 (10-Q Q3 page:2).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: For Mativ Holdings, Inc. the creditor-relevant facts are these. It is a publicly listed Delaware company (NYSE: MATV) that has been independent since a 1995 spin-off from Kimberly-Clark and took its current form on July 6, 2022 when Schweitzer-Mauduit International merged with Neenah and renamed itself Mativ. Its 2023 sale of the Engineered Papers business for 620.0 in cash ended participation in tobacco-based product markets and was followed by a debt repayment of about 641.2 that the 10-K ties to a covenant trigger. There is no sponsor, and no controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied text (Part III of the 10-K is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not in the sources), so ownership behaviour can only be judged from documented issuer actions.

There is no sponsor, and no controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied text (Part III of the 10-K is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not in the sources), so ownership behaviour can only be judged from documented issuer actions.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Operating model: two reportable segments, Filtration & Advanced Materials (FAM, about 39 percent of FY2025 revenue) and Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions (SAS, about 61 percent), serve dozens of end markets through 34 production locations on three continents and sales in more than 100 countries, with roughly 57 percent of Q3 2026 net sales to U.S. customers and 25 percent to Europe. The risk mechanics that matter to a creditor are: pricing power against resin, fiber, pulp and energy inputs (selling prices rose in 2026 while volume and mix fell), a weakening SAS volume position in Q3 2026 (tornado and Healthcare) set against FAM growth, a margin structure in which FAM earns materially higher gross margin than SAS, and a funding model that sells receivables off balance sheet and relies on a revolver that is now 305.0. Credit implication: revenue is diversified and customer-qualified, which supports durability, but gross margin of roughly 19.6 percent for nine months 2026 and reported-basis interest cover of 2.62x leave little room for a volume shock; the July 27, 2026 tornado showed that a single third-party distribution node can interrupt supply for a whole product line.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The one financing transaction in the period is the Ninth Amendment of April 3, 2026 to the 2018 multicurrency credit agreement (the ninth amendment, after an Eighth Amendment dated December 17, 2024). Status: executed, effective April 3, 2026, reported in the 10-Q Q1 as a subsequent event and in the 10-Q Q2 and Q3 as completed (10-Q Q1 page:21; 10-Q Q3 page:13). It provided a 305.0 revolving facility with euro and sterling sub-facilities, an 89.9 Term Loan A and a 500.0 Term Loan B, 894.9 of committed facilities in total, and eliminated the delayed draw term loan. Use of proceeds is shown in the cash flow statement: nine-month debt proceeds of 705.7 against repayments of 728.1, 32.7 of issuance costs and an 8.7 loss on debt extinguishment. The revolver and Term Loan A mature on the earlier of five years from April 3, 2026 or 182 days before the notes' maturity, and the Term Loan B on the earlier of seven years or 91 days before it; certain subsidiaries became additional U.S. borrowers and another a guarantor (names not supplied). The Term Loan B pays fixed margins of 3.50 to 4.50 percent depending on the benchmark, against 2.75 percent over Term SOFR and 3.75 percent over EURIBOR in the 10-K description of the prior agreement, which reads as roughly 75 basis points more at the stated ends, although the 10-Q does not say which end applies to which benchmark. This is an Analyst Interpretation. Liquidity effect: revolver availability dropped from 416.2 (old 600.0 facility, March 31, 2026) to 279.2 at June 30, 2026, and total liquidity from 498.5 to 345.5, in exchange for the removal of the May 2027 maturity wall (10-K page:103 shows 514.2 of maturities in 2027).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Mativ Holdings, Inc. is a leveraged but liquid specialty materials credit whose fundamental strength is adequate and improving, not yet comfortable. Its strongest support is a refinanced capital structure with no material maturity before the USD 400.0 million 8.000% notes due October 1, 2029, USD 373.5 million of liquidity and compliance with a net leverage covenant that stands at 3.8x against a 5.00x maximum. Its weakest point is thin earnings coverage: on reported earnings net debt is 4.19x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.62x, while the largest segment by revenue, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, earns the lower gross margin and lost volume in the third quarter of 2026. The outcome turns on whether price-led margin recovery and cost savings hold as volume weakens, and on refinancing the 2029 notes.

Its weakest point is thin earnings coverage: on reported earnings net debt is 4.19x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.62x, while the largest segment by revenue, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, earns the lower gross margin and lost volume in the third quarter of 2026. The outcome turns on whether price-led margin recovery and cost savings hold as volume weakens, and on refinancing the 2029 notes.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the refinancing changed the shape of the debt more than its size. On April 3, 2026 Mativ replaced its revolver, Term Loan A and Term Loan B and removed the delayed draw term loan, which took away the May 2027 maturity wall (about USD 514.2 million at year-end 2025) [CP-1 debt register; CP-1A transaction summary]. Total debt carrying value is USD 976.4 million and net debt USD 879.1 million, against USD 1,018.2 million and USD 934.0 million at December 31, 2025. The mechanic is that the nearest large repayment is now the notes, which with small amortization make up USD 406.2 million of the USD 1,011.1 million of principal due in 2029 on the maturity table, about 40.2 percent [CP-1 debt maturities chart; calculated below]. The implication is low near-term repayment risk and a concentrated 2029 refinancing, with an eight percent coupon already in the cost of debt. One wording in the credit agreement could pull the revolver and Term Loan A (USD 109.7 million drawn and outstanding) ahead of the notes, which would lift the 2029 bucket to about 51.0 percent of principal; the filing's own maturity table does not show this, and the amended agreement is needed to settle it [CP-0 and CP-1 conflicts].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, leverage depends on whose earnings are used, and the deleveraging has mostly come from earnings, not debt paydown. Management states net leverage of 3.8x at September 30, 2026 against 5.00x allowed, down from 4.2x at December 31, 2025 [CP-1 covenants]. On reported operating profit plus depreciation and amortization, net debt to EBITDA fell from 5.54x to 4.19x, and holding net debt at the year-end level would have given 4.45x, so about 1.09x of the 1.35x improvement came from higher trailing EBITDA (USD 168.5 million to USD 210.0 million) and about 0.26x from lower net debt [calculated below]. The mechanic is that trailing EBITDA rose partly because restructuring and impairment charges fell (nine months 2026 USD 4.7 million against USD 18.2 million) and partly on margin recovery; both can reverse. The implication is that leverage headroom today is comfortable (EBITDA could fall about 24.0 percent before 5.00x at constant net debt) but narrows toward the final 4.00x step, where the same measure gives about 5.0 percent, and the step dates are not disclosed [CP-1 covenants].

facts.text: Fourth, the earnings mix is shifting toward the higher-margin segment while the larger segment weakens. Filtration & Advanced Materials grew net sales 10.2 percent in Q3 2026 with a gross margin of 23.6 percent, while Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions fell 10.9 percent at a gross margin of 16.4 percent, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 62.3 million fell about 7 percent against USD 66.8 million a year earlier [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model]. Price added 3.7 percent to Q3 sales while volume and mix removed 5.9 percent, so margin recovery has come from pricing, not volume. The mechanic is dependence on input-cost pass-through and demand in cyclical end markets, with Healthcare weak. The implication is that a further volume loss would flow disproportionately into earnings and cover.

Trailing free cash flow of about USD 98.5 million after USD 22.5 million of dividends leaves about USD 76.0 million a year, so if that were held flat to October 2029 it would retire about 57 percent of the USD 400.0 million notes [calculated below, assumption stated]. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The business is diversified: no product category exceeds 35 percent of sales and no customer exceeds 10 percent, which supports revenue durability through cycles [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. The capital structure is refinanced, with the nearest large maturity in October 2029, covenant compliance stated at September 30, 2026 and liquidity of USD 373.5 million [CP-1 liquidity and debt register; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation covers capital spending and the dividend: nine-month free cash flow was USD 90.5 million (a management measure) against dividends of USD 17.0 million [CP-1 cash flow; Documentary Fact]. Filtration & Advanced Materials is gaining profitability, with adjusted EBITDA of USD 39.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 32.9 million, and management targets further cost savings of USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million by end 2026 [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact for the first, Management Language for the target]. About two thirds of floating bank debt is hedged with interest rate swaps (USD 405.8 million notional against USD 608.4 million of floating balances), limiting rate sensitivity [CP-1A operating model; Analyst Interpretation on the ratio]. Reporting quality is sound, with effective internal control and no related-party or priming-type transaction found [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact].

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: - Deleveraging attribution: net debt to EBITDA at FY2025 is 934.0 / 168.5 = 5.54x; at Q3 2026 it is 879.1 / 210.0 = 4.19x; improvement 5.54 - 4.19 = 1.35x. Holding net debt at 934.0 and using the Q3 2026 EBITDA gives 934.0 / 210.0 = 4.45x. The EBITDA effect is 5.54 - 4.45 = 1.09x (from EBITDA rising by (210.0 - 168.5) / 168.5 = 24.6 percent); the net debt effect is 4.45 - 4.19 = 0.26x (net debt down 934.0 - 879.1 = 54.9, or 5.9 percent). The attribution depends on the FY2025 base, which carried 19.9 of restructuring and other impairment charges. - Principal concentration in 2029: notes 400.0 / principal 1,011.1 = 39.6 percent; 2029 bucket on the table 406.2 / 1,011.1 = 40.2 percent. If revolver 20.0 and Term Loan A 89.7 (sum 109.7) matured in 2029, the bucket is 406.2 + 109.7 = 515.9, or 515.9 / 1,011.1 = 51.0 percent. Inputs from the debt register and maturity table (CP-1). - Free cash flow capacity (assumption: trailing figures held flat, no growth, no working-capital swing): trailing management-basis free cash flow 98.5 less trailing dividends 22.5 = 76.0 a year; over the 3.0 years from September 30, 2026 to October 1, 2029 that is 76.0 x 3 = 228.0, or 228.0 / 400.0 = 57 percent of the notes. This is an illustrative projection, not a forecast; free cash flow benefited from a working-capital inflow and a tax refund (CP-1). - Free cash flow to debt: 98.5 / 976.4 = 10.1 percent. - Interest cover headroom over the covenant floor: reported-basis cover 2.62x less 2.50x = 0.12x, equal to an EBITDA fall of 1 - 2.50 / 2.62 = 4.6 percent at constant interest; this is a proxy only because the covenant uses different definitions. - Covenant EBITDA cushion at constant net debt (CP-1): 1 - 3.8 / 5.00 = 24.0 percent; 1 - 3.8 / 4.00 = 5.0 percent. - Insurance receivable relative to cash: 38.0 / 97.3 = 39.1 percent. - Adjusted EBITDA change in Q3 2026: (62.3 - 66.8) / 66.8 = -6.7 percent (the release prints "down 7%").

facts.label: Evidence trace view
facts.text: The credit analysis for Mativ Holdings, Inc. is traceable enough for restricted committee use. Every one of the 58 key inputs checked is printed on the page the handoffs cite, the derived leverage, interest cover, liquidity, maturity and free cash flow figures recompute exactly, and the same figure carries the same value in every handoff that uses it. Of 20 material claims, 10 are directly sourced, 5 calculated, 1 assumption-based and 4 analyst inference. ### Readiness view

Overall view: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the requested module set. The registrant is a single reporting entity, Mativ Holdings, Inc., filing consolidated statements for itself and its subsidiaries; there is no parent, sponsor or separate borrower reporting entity in the supplied evidence, so the perimeter question that arises for subsidiary issuers does not arise here. The latest annual report (FY2025, filed with an audit opinion and an effective internal control opinion, 10-K page:121 and page:125) and the three 2026 quarterly reports give a continuous filed-statement series from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026. The three earnings releases supply attributed management measures (adjusted EBITDA, adjusted income, free cash flow, net debt, liquidity) that no filing in the pack supplies. These are supporting claims; the filed statements control where both speak to the same fact.

Strongest contrary evidence and limits: (1) the governing financing documents (the Ninth Amendment to the credit agreement of April 3, 2026, the indenture for the 8.000% senior notes due October 1, 2029, the receivables purchase agreement and its October 23, 2026 amendment) are only summarized in notes, so definitions, baskets, covenant step-down dates and guarantor lists cannot be read at source; (2) none of the periodic reports prints adjusted EBITDA and the releases cover only the first three quarters of 2026 with 2025 comparatives, so an annual or trailing figure is not available from supplied inputs and the stated net leverage cannot be reproduced; (3) no credit ratings, presentations, call transcripts or market quotes are supplied. Evidence-to-risk-to-consequence: the missing legal text means the downstream financial module can state covenant levels as management and note disclosures describe them but cannot test definitions; the missing annual adjusted figure means downstream leverage must be shown on reported-debt and reported-GAAP bases with management's figure attributed.

What cannot proceed: any analysis that depends on reading the financing documents themselves is outside what this pack can support and is not part of the requested set; relative value, market pricing and rating-based views are likewise outside the supplied evidence. What can proceed: all four requested modules, per the consumer table below. Next evidence action: add the credit agreement as amended and the indenture (both filed as exhibits per the 10-K and Q1 10-Q exhibit lists), the fourth quarter 2025 earnings release, and any rating agency publications, if the committee needs covenant headroom or a trailing adjusted leverage figure.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Reported leverage has fallen since the April 2026 refinancing, but on a reported earnings basis it is still above four times and interest cover is thin. Liquidity is adequate, though the revolver is smaller. | Medium | Management leverage uses an adjusted earnings definition and agreement text that are not in the sources, so covenant headroom cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| The April 2026 refinancing pushed the bank maturities out and removed the 2027 wall, leaving the 8.000% notes due 2029 as the main bullet. | Near-term refinancing risk is low, but a 2029 refinancing of the notes is the key event. | Medium |

| Net debt fell and management reports net leverage of 3.8x against a 5.00x maximum that steps down toward 4.00x. | Headroom is comfortable today and thins at the final step-down, whose timing is not supplied. | Medium |

| On reported earnings the trailing interest cover is 2.62x on cash interest, and the quarter was hit by the July tornado. | Cover is modest, and most of the insured inventory loss is still a receivable rather than cash. | Medium |
| Cash flow is positive but leans on receivable sales, a tax refund and a working capital inflow. | Cash generation quality is weaker than the headline free cash flow suggests. | Medium |
### Financial base view

For Mativ Holdings, Inc. the financial base at September 30, 2026 is a company with USD 1,510.9 million of nine-month net sales (nine months 2026), gross profit up year on year for the nine months (though down in Q3), a thin operating margin and a net loss close to break-even for the nine months (net loss of 9.3 against a prior-year loss of 438.2 that carried an 411.9 goodwill impairment), financed by 976.4 of total debt (carrying value, net of 34.7 issuance costs; principal 1,011.1) against cash and cash equivalents of 97.3, so reported net debt of 879.1. The structure was reset on April 3, 2026 by the Ninth Amendment: a 305.0 revolver (20.0 drawn), an 89.9 Term Loan A, a 500.0 Term Loan B and the unchanged 400.0 of 8.000% senior unsecured notes due October 1, 2029. Management states net leverage of 3.8x at September 30, 2026 against a current maximum of 5.00x, down from 4.2x at December 31, 2025 and 4.1x at March 31, 2026.

The reported-basis measures built here are lower quality than management's: operating profit plus depreciation and amortization (with the 411.9 FY2025 goodwill impairment added back) gives trailing EBITDA of 210.0 at Q3 2026, so total debt to EBITDA is 4.65x and net debt to EBITDA is 4.19x, with EBITDA to cash interest of 2.62x. These are above management's 3.8x because the credit agreement and management adjusted EBITDA add back items such as stock compensation, restructuring, financing fees on the receivables program and purchase-accounting items; that definition is not supplied, so the two cannot be reconciled and neither is restated into the other. Evidence to risk to implication: a lender that sizes debt on the adjusted figure sees a levered but compliant credit; a lender that sizes it on reported earnings sees a leverage multiple that only recently dropped below five times, which makes the 2029 notes refinancing and the covenant step-downs the focus.

Liquidity is cash of 97.3 plus printed undrawn revolver capacity of 276.2, total 373.5, down from 498.5 at March 31, 2026 because the revolver was cut from 600.0 to 305.0. On the maturity table's reading nothing in the debt falls due before 2029 except 2.2 in the rest of 2026 and small amortization. Claims outside the debt figure are meaningful: a receivables sale program (837.3 sold in nine months 2026, balance outstanding not supplied), a foreign exchange contract liability of 27.6 in other liabilities (the euro cross-currency swap hedges are disclosed alongside), pension and other postretirement liabilities of 49.1, operating leases of 56.2, finance leases of 14.7 non-current, purchase obligations of 105.1 at year-end 2025, and open insurance recovery on the July 27, 2026 Menasha tornado (expense of 43.8 less recoveries received 5.0 and receivable 38.0, leaving a 0.8 net loss recorded). The view is restricted by the absence of the credit agreement, the indenture, the receivables agreement and any annual adjusted EBITDA.

### Business and transaction view

For Mativ Holdings, Inc. the creditor-relevant facts are these. It is a publicly listed Delaware company (NYSE: MATV) that has been independent since a 1995 spin-off from Kimberly-Clark and took its current form on July 6, 2022 when Schweitzer-Mauduit International merged with Neenah and renamed itself Mativ. Its 2023 sale of the Engineered Papers business for 620.0 in cash ended participation in tobacco-based product markets and was followed by a debt repayment of about 641.2 that the 10-K ties to a covenant trigger. There is no sponsor, and no controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied text (Part III of the 10-K is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not in the sources), so ownership behaviour can only be judged from documented issuer actions.

Operating model: two reportable segments, Filtration & Advanced Materials (FAM, about 39 percent of FY2025 revenue) and Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions (SAS, about 61 percent), serve dozens of end markets through 34 production locations on three continents and sales in more than 100 countries, with roughly 57 percent of Q3 2026 net sales to U.S. customers and 25 percent to Europe. The risk mechanics that matter to a creditor are: pricing power against resin, fiber, pulp and energy inputs (selling prices rose in 2026 while volume and mix fell), a weakening SAS volume position in Q3 2026 (tornado and Healthcare) set against FAM growth, a margin structure in which FAM earns materially higher gross margin than SAS, and a funding model that sells receivables off balance sheet and relies on a revolver that is now 305.0. Credit implication: revenue is diversified and customer-qualified, which supports durability, but gross margin of roughly 19.6 percent for nine months 2026 and reported-basis interest cover of 2.62x leave little room for a volume shock; the July 27, 2026 tornado showed that a single third-party distribution node can interrupt supply for a whole product line.

Transactions: the April 3, 2026 Ninth Amendment refinanced the entire bank group (revolver cut from 600.0 to 305.0, Term Loan A 89.9, Term Loan B 500.0, delayed draw term loan removed, maturities moved from May 2027 to 2031 and 2033 on the stated terms, subject to a springing wording that is unresolved against the maturity table). The 400.0 of 8.000% senior unsecured notes issued in October 2024 are the nearest maturity on the company's own statements (October 1, 2029). The interaction between the term loan B's size and the covenant scope is the main structural point: the maintenance covenants are stated to apply to the revolver and Term Loan A only, so the 500.0 Term Loan B lenders hold no maintenance test of their own. Restrictions on information: the credit agreement, indenture and receivables agreement are not supplied, so baskets, guarantor coverage and restricted payment capacity are Not supplied.

It builds the fundamental credit view from the financial and business handoffs already accepted, for the reporting currency USD and the periods Q3 2026 and FY2025. Refinancing and liquidity support it; thin earnings coverage and the 2029 notes are the pressure points. | Medium | The financing documents and an annual adjusted earnings figure are missing, so covenant headroom and management's leverage cannot be tested. |

### Credit view

Mativ Holdings, Inc. is a leveraged but liquid specialty materials credit whose fundamental strength is adequate and improving, not yet comfortable. Its strongest support is a refinanced capital structure with no material maturity before the USD 400.0 million 8.000% notes due October 1, 2029, USD 373.5 million of liquidity and compliance with a net leverage covenant that stands at 3.8x against a 5.00x maximum. Its weakest point is thin earnings coverage: on reported earnings net debt is 4.19x EBITDA and EBITDA covers cash interest only 2.62x, while the largest segment by revenue, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, earns the lower gross margin and lost volume in the third quarter of 2026. The outcome turns on whether price-led margin recovery and cost savings hold as volume weakens, and on refinancing the 2029 notes.
### Key findings

First, the refinancing changed the shape of the debt more than its size. On April 3, 2026 Mativ replaced its revolver, Term Loan A and Term Loan B and removed the delayed draw term loan, which took away the May 2027 maturity wall (about USD 514.2 million at year-end 2025) [CP-1 debt register; CP-1A transaction summary]. Total debt carrying value is USD 976.4 million and net debt USD 879.1 million, against USD 1,018.2 million and USD 934.0 million at December 31, 2025. The mechanic is that the nearest large repayment is now the notes, which with small amortization make up USD 406.2 million of the USD 1,011.1 million of principal due in 2029 on the maturity table, about 40.2 percent [CP-1 debt maturities chart; calculated below]. The implication is low near-term repayment risk and a concentrated 2029 refinancing, with an eight percent coupon already in the cost of debt. One wording in the credit agreement could pull the revolver and Term Loan A (USD 109.7 million drawn and outstanding) ahead of the notes, which would lift the 2029 bucket to about 51.0 percent of principal; the filing's own maturity table does not show this, and the amended agreement is needed to settle it [CP-0 and CP-1 conflicts].

Second, leverage depends on whose earnings are used, and the deleveraging has mostly come from earnings, not debt paydown. Management states net leverage of 3.8x at September 30, 2026 against 5.00x allowed, down from 4.2x at December 31, 2025 [CP-1 covenants]. On reported operating profit plus depreciation and amortization, net debt to EBITDA fell from 5.54x to 4.19x, and holding net debt at the year-end level would have given 4.45x, so about 1.09x of the 1.35x improvement came from higher trailing EBITDA (USD 168.5 million to USD 210.0 million) and about 0.26x from lower net debt [calculated below]. The mechanic is that trailing EBITDA rose partly because restructuring and impairment charges fell (nine months 2026 USD 4.7 million against USD 18.2 million) and partly on margin recovery; both can reverse. The implication is that leverage headroom today is comfortable (EBITDA could fall about 24.0 percent before 5.00x at constant net debt) but narrows toward the final 4.00x step, where the same measure gives about 5.0 percent, and the step dates are not disclosed [CP-1 covenants].

Third, interest cover is thin on reported earnings. EBITDA covers cash interest 2.62x over the last twelve months and interest expense 2.92x, only 0.12x above the lowest covenant level of 2.50x and below the 3.00x top level, although covenant EBITDA and interest are defined differently and the reported coverage ratio is not disclosed [CP-1 interest cover chart; CP-1 covenants]. Management's own nine-month adjusted EBITDA over cash interest is 3.52x. The mechanic is a fixed interest burden of about USD 80.1 million of cash interest on earnings that move with volume; the implication is limited cushion if the third-quarter volume decline persists.

Fourth, the earnings mix is shifting toward the higher-margin segment while the larger segment weakens. Filtration & Advanced Materials grew net sales 10.2 percent in Q3 2026 with a gross margin of 23.6 percent, while Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions fell 10.9 percent at a gross margin of 16.4 percent, and adjusted EBITDA of USD 62.3 million fell about 7 percent against USD 66.8 million a year earlier [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model]. Price added 3.7 percent to Q3 sales while volume and mix removed 5.9 percent, so margin recovery has come from pricing, not volume. The mechanic is dependence on input-cost pass-through and demand in cyclical end markets, with Healthcare weak. The implication is that a further volume loss would flow disproportionately into earnings and cover.

Fifth, liquidity is adequate but less deep than before and partly dependent on off-balance-sheet funding. Liquidity of USD 373.5 million is cash of USD 97.3 million (USD 72.7 million held abroad) plus printed undrawn revolver capacity of USD 276.2 million, down from USD 498.5 million in March 2026 because the revolver was reduced to USD 305.0 million; USD 8.8 million of commitment is unexplained [CP-1 liquidity]. Trailing free cash flow of about USD 98.5 million after USD 22.5 million of dividends leaves about USD 76.0 million a year, so if that were held flat to October 2029 it would retire about 57 percent of the USD 400.0 million notes [calculated below, assumption stated]. The company sold USD 837.3 million of receivables in nine months 2026 under a program extended to October 23, 2029, and carries leases, pensions and a foreign exchange contract liability outside reported debt [CP-1 claims outside debt]. The implication is that the notes will need refinancing and that withdrawal of the receivables program would need replacement from the revolver.

Sixth, the July 27, 2026 tornado left USD 38.0 million of insurance recoveries receivable (about 39 percent of cash) and a net recorded loss of USD 0.8 million; business interruption recoveries are not recognized. The mechanic is delayed cash on an insured loss and a single third-party distribution node that interrupted supply; the implication is a near-term liquidity watch item, with management expecting full recovery of the inventory loss [CP-1 events; CP-1A operating model, Management Language].

Seventh, creditor protection cannot be read directly. The maintenance covenants are stated to apply to the revolver and Term Loan A only, so the USD 498.7 million Term Loan B carries none; the credit agreement, indenture and receivables agreement are not in the evidence, so baskets, guarantor coverage, security after the amendment and distribution capacity are unknown. Documented actions show no related-party, priming or non-pro rata transactions and a smaller dividend than in 2023 [CP-1A governance]. The implication is a supportive willingness record but an untested legal capacity.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The business is diversified: no product category exceeds 35 percent of sales and no customer exceeds 10 percent, which supports revenue durability through cycles [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. The capital structure is refinanced, with the nearest large maturity in October 2029, covenant compliance stated at September 30, 2026 and liquidity of USD 373.5 million [CP-1 liquidity and debt register; Documentary Fact]. Cash generation covers capital spending and the dividend: nine-month free cash flow was USD 90.5 million (a management measure) against dividends of USD 17.0 million [CP-1 cash flow; Documentary Fact]. Filtration & Advanced Materials is gaining profitability, with adjusted EBITDA of USD 39.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 32.9 million, and management targets further cost savings of USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million by end 2026 [CP-1 segments; CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact for the first, Management Language for the target]. About two thirds of floating bank debt is hedged with interest rate swaps (USD 405.8 million notional against USD 608.4 million of floating balances), limiting rate sensitivity [CP-1A operating model; Analyst Interpretation on the ratio]. Reporting quality is sound, with effective internal control and no related-party or priming-type transaction found [CP-1A governance; Documentary Fact].

Weaknesses. Reported leverage and cover are tight: net debt to EBITDA of 4.19x and EBITDA to cash interest of 2.62x on reported earnings, with total debt to capital at 67.6 percent [CP-1 leverage and covenants; Documentary Fact for inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]. Margins are low and recovered through price while volume and mix fell, with the larger segment, Sustainable & Adhesive Solutions, at a lower gross margin and showing a 10.9 percent sales decline in Q3 2026 [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. Refinancing is back-ended: the USD 400.0 million notes at 8.000% fall due on October 1, 2029, and a possible earlier maturity of the revolver and Term Loan A is unresolved [CP-1 debt maturities; Documentary Fact and Insufficient Information]. Funding relies on a receivables program that is off balance sheet and on claims outside reported debt, including operating leases of USD 56.2 million, pension and other postretirement liabilities of USD 49.1 million and a foreign exchange contract liability of USD 27.6 million [CP-1 claims outside debt; Documentary Fact]. Operating concentration was demonstrated by the tornado, and Healthcare volume is weak [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact].
### Credit assessment
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Adequate and improving fundamental credit strength with thin earnings cover and a concentrated 2029 refinancing; no near-term liquidity stress on the evidence | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, interest cover, liquidity, debt maturities; CP-1A operating model and transaction summary |

| Thesis | Mativ is a refinanced, adequately liquid but thinly covered specialty materials issuer whose credit quality will be decided by whether earnings recovery outlasts the volume decline before the October 2029 notes fall due | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | Same basis |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Refinancing of the 2029 notes and a possible earlier bank maturity | A bullet equal to about 40 percent of principal, possibly 51 percent, requires market access | Medium-term repayment and refinancing cost risk | Material |

| Thin interest cover and covenant step-down | Fixed cash interest of about USD 80.1 million against earnings that move with volume; maximum leverage steps down toward 4.00x | Reduced headroom if EBITDA weakens | Material |
| Price-led margins with falling volume | Input-cost pass-through and cyclical end markets; Healthcare and tornado-hit paper and packaging volume weak | Earnings and cover volatility | Material |

| Off-balance-sheet funding and claims outside debt | Receivables sales of USD 837.3 million in nine months, leases, pensions and a foreign exchange contract liability sit outside reported debt | Leverage understated if funding is withdrawn or claims crystallize | Material |
| Opaque creditor protection | Legal documents absent; Term Loan B has no maintenance covenant | Cannot assess creditor control or capacity for creditor-adverse actions | Material |
| Operating concentration and insurance recovery | A third-party distribution site destroyed; USD 38.0 million receivable not yet collected | Temporary supply and liquidity strain | Minor |
| Floating-rate exposure | About USD 202.6 million of floating bank debt is unhedged | Interest cost sensitivity | Minor |
## Calculations

All amounts USD millions unless stated. Inputs come from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs; each calculation is repeated here so it can be recomputed. The reported-basis EBITDA of 168.5 (FY2025) and 210.0 (twelve months to September 30, 2026) is the CP-1 construction: operating profit plus depreciation and amortization, with the FY2025 goodwill impairment of 411.9 added back.

- Deleveraging attribution: net debt to EBITDA at FY2025 is 934.0 / 168.5 = 5.54x; at Q3 2026 it is 879.1 / 210.0 = 4.19x; improvement 5.54 - 4.19 = 1.35x. Holding net debt at 934.0 and using the Q3 2026 EBITDA gives 934.0 / 210.0 = 4.45x. The EBITDA effect is 5.54 - 4.45 = 1.09x (from EBITDA rising by (210.0 - 168.5) / 168.5 = 24.6 percent); the net debt effect is 4.45 - 4.19 = 0.26x (net debt down 934.0 - 879.1 = 54.9, or 5.9 percent). The attribution depends on the FY2025 base, which carried 19.9 of restructuring and other impairment charges.

- Principal concentration in 2029: notes 400.0 / principal 1,011.1 = 39.6 percent; 2029 bucket on the table 406.2 / 1,011.1 = 40.2 percent. If revolver 20.0 and Term Loan A 89.7 (sum 109.7) matured in 2029, the bucket is 406.2 + 109.7 = 515.9, or 515.9 / 1,011.1 = 51.0 percent. Inputs from the debt register and maturity table (CP-1).

- Free cash flow capacity (assumption: trailing figures held flat, no growth, no working-capital swing): trailing management-basis free cash flow 98.5 less trailing dividends 22.5 = 76.0 a year; over the 3.0 years from September 30, 2026 to October 1, 2029 that is 76.0 x 3 = 228.0, or 228.0 / 400.0 = 57 percent of the notes. This is an illustrative projection, not a forecast; free cash flow benefited from a working-capital inflow and a tax refund (CP-1).
- Free cash flow to debt: 98.5 / 976.4 = 10.1 percent.

- Interest cover headroom over the covenant floor: reported-basis cover 2.62x less 2.50x = 0.12x, equal to an EBITDA fall of 1 - 2.50 / 2.62 = 4.6 percent at constant interest; this is a proxy only because the covenant uses different definitions.
- Covenant EBITDA cushion at constant net debt (CP-1): 1 - 3.8 / 5.00 = 24.0 percent; 1 - 3.8 / 4.00 = 5.0 percent.
- Insurance receivable relative to cash: 38.0 / 97.3 = 39.1 percent.
- Adjusted EBITDA change in Q3 2026: (62.3 - 66.8) / 66.8 = -6.7 percent (the release prints "down 7%").

Not supplied does not mean zero for any item above. No recovery conclusion, peer ranking or instrument recommendation is made; legal-capacity statements are Insufficient Information.
## Next module

It should check that each figure in this handoff matches the financial handoff exactly (leverage 4.19x and 2.62x, liquidity USD 373.5 million, the 2029 bucket of USD 406.2 million, management's 3.8x) and that every business claim rests on a tagged business fact; that the attribution, concentration and free cash flow calculations recompute from their inputs; and that Management Language rows (cost-savings target, expected insurance recovery, segment growth claims) were not adopted as fact.
